small_guidance: Hoist the `for ic` loop OUT of the kd/kh/kw loops and accumulate per (kd,kh,kw) into a single acc register tile, but better: swap loop order so the inner GEMM-K is IC (reduction) with acc held in registers; pre-load all IC input values for sp_offs once per spatial tile (IC=16 fits) then iterate KD*KH*KW reusing those loads. Also drop atomic_add by making the grid iterate over OUTPUT positions (gather) instead of input (scatter) — each output is written exactly once. Try BLOCK_OC=32, BLOCK_SP=64, num_warps=4, num_stages=2 to reduce the 128 regs/thread that is capping occupancy at 33%.
large_guidance: Redesign as a gather-style implicit-GEMM ConvTranspose3d: one program per (N, OC-tile, output-spatial-tile). For each output voxel (od,oh,ow), compute which (id,ih,iw,kd,kh,kw) input/kernel pairs map to it (the standard transposed-conv index math: id=(od+PD-kd)/SD when divisible), build a K-dimension of size IC*#valid_taps, and run a tl.dot against a [IC*KDKHKW, OC] weight matrix view. This eliminates atomics (current scatter does atomic_add into 200MB output → 86% memory throughput bottleneck and double-write traffic), enables tl.dot tensor-core use (currently compute_throughput=21%), and lets BatchNorm+mean-subtract fuse into the same epilogue: accumulate per-channel sum across the output tile, do a second pass that subtracts the (precomputed) per-(n,c) mean. Fold BN running stats into scale/shift at init. Use channels-last output layout so OC is the contiguous GEMM-N.
